system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
The graph shows the number of pens, pencils, rulers, and erasers sold by a store in one week.

[Image: Bar graph of items sold]

The names of the items are missing from the graph. Pens were the item most often sold, and fewer erasers than any other item were sold. More pencils than rulers were sold. How many pencils were sold?

Figure, described in words:
A vertical bar graph. The vertical axis is labeled "Number of Items" with tick marks and numbers at increments of 20 from 0 up to 160 (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 160). The horizontal axis is labeled "Items Sold by Store". There are four shaded vertical bars without individual category labels beneath them. From left to right, their heights are:
- First bar: 120
- Second bar: 80
- Third bar: 140
- Fourth bar: 40

A. 40
B. 80
C. 120
D. 140

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
answer.title: Answer

llm_thinking: With bars of 120, 80, 140, and 40, pens are clearly the most sold at 140 and erasers the fewest at 40. Since pencils must outnumber rulers, pencils take the 120 value and rulers the 80, confirming answer C.
